Description: This recall involves Bodum 8-cup and 12-cup Bistro, Brazil, Caffettiera, Chambord, Crema, Java, Jesper, and Kenya model French Press coffee makers with replaceable glass carafes. The Bodum name appears on the frame and inner lid of most models, and is engraved, along with product warnings, on the glass carafes. Additional photos and model-identifying information are available on the recall website.
Title: Bodum USA Recalls 5.9 Million French Press Coffee Makers with Replaceable Glass Carafes Due to Risk of Serious Burn Injury
ConsumerContact: Bodum USA toll-free at 888-879-8213 from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. ET Monday through Friday, email at Bodum3302@sedgwick.com, or online at www.bodumfrenchpressrecall.expertinquiry.com or www.bodum.com  and click on “Recall Information” for more information.

Products.Name: Bodum French Press coffee makers with 8-cup and 12-cup replaceable glass carafes (Bistro, Brazil, Caffettiera, Chambord, Crema, Java, Jesper, and Kenya models)

Images.Caption: Identifying text on Bodum French Press Carafe

Injuries.Name: Bodum USA has identified 70 reports of carafes breaking during use, including 48 reports of burns to consumers

Retailers.Name:
Sold At:
Target, Walmart, and coffee and home goods stores nationwide and online at Bodum.com, Amazon.com, Target.com, Walmart.com and other online retailers from 1974 through October 2026 for about $15 to $65.

Importers.Name: Bodum USA, Inc., of New York, New York

Hazards.Name: The carafe can unexpectedly break during use if the glass carafe is damaged or cracked, including by use of a metal spoon to stir the coffee, posing a risk of serious burn injuries.

Remedies.Name: Consumers should stop using metal spoons or utensils to stir coffee in the glass carafe immediately and contact Bodum to receive a plastic Bodum stirring spoon and warning label. The label reminds consumers not to use cracked or damaged carafes and not to use metal spoons to stir contents in the glass carafe in order to avoid damaging the glass, which can lead to breakage during use.

Description: This recall involves NTI brand residential gas boilers in the FTVN and TFTN model series, and HTP brand residential gas boilers in the EFTU model series. The NTI FTVN and TFTN series boilers are gray, while the HTP EFTU (Elite Fire Tube Ultra) boilers are black. The boilers are metal, rectangular units and have either NTI or HTP printed on the front. The model serial number can be found on the rating plate, located on the left-hand side of the boiler. The following models and serial number ranges are included in this recall:
Title: NTI and HTP Brand Gas Boilers Recalled Due to Risk of Serious Injury or Death from Fire, Carbon Monoxide (CO) Poisoning and Impact Hazards; Manufactured by Ariston, formerly NTI Boilers
ConsumerContact: Ariston at 800-688-2575 from 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. ET Monday through Friday, email at VCexchanger@ariston.com or online at https://ntiboilers.com/safety-recalls or www.ntiboilers.com and click on “RECALLS” at the top of the page or https://htproducts.com/safety-notice.html or www.htproducts.com and click on “URGENT RECALL” at the top of the page for more information.

Products.Name: NTI and HTP residential gas boilers

Images.Caption: Recalled NTI and HTP Brand Gas Boilers

Injuries.Name: The firm has received 34 reported incidents of the condensate dish breaking, including three reports of the front cover detaching from the boiler. In one reported incident the technician servicing the boiler sustained a broken jaw.

Manufacturers.Name: Ariston Canada Inc. (Formerly NTI Boilers Inc.), of Canada

Retailers.Name:
Sold At:
Independent heating and plumbing contractors and wholesale distributors nationwide from May 2021 through July 2026 for between $3,200 and $7,700.

Importers.Name: Ariston Thermo USA LLC, of Providence, Rhode Island

Hazards.Name: The condensate dish inside the boiler can crack during a delayed ignition, allowing unburned gas to build up inside the sealed cabinet. If the gas ignites, the front cover can suddenly detach, posing a risk of serious injury or death from fire, carbon monoxide (CO) poisoning, and impact hazards.

Remedies.Name: Consumers should stop using the recalled boilers immediately and contact Ariston to schedule a free repair by a certified technician. Consumers who must continue using the boiler while awaiting repair should have working smoke and carbon monoxide alarms in their homes.

Description: These DeWalt 7 1/4-inch framing saws have model number DW378G, which is located on a black name plate on the side of the saw. These saws have date codes 9813F through 9820F, located on the bottom of the saw below the power cord. The saws are yellow with black accents and have a silver-colored blade guard. "DEWALT" is written on the blade guard.
Title: CPSC, DeWalt Announce Recall to Repair Framing Saws
ConsumerContact: To locate the nearest service center or for more information, consumers should call DeWalt toll-free at (888) 839-3559 between 8 a.m. and 4:30 p.m. EST Monday through Friday.

Injuries.Name: DeWalt is aware of 15 reports of the saw's lower blade guard failing to fully close. Of these incidents, there have been eight reports of lacerations, with at least three cases requiring stitches.

Manufacturers.Name: DeWalt Industrial Tool Co., of Hampstead, Md.

Retailers.Name: Major home centers and hardware stores, as well as local hardware stores, sold these saws nationwide, from May 1998 through September 1998, for between $149 and $175.

Hazards.Name: The saw's lower blade guard can fail to fully close during use, leaving the blade exposed and presenting a risk of laceration.

Remedies.Name: Consumers should immediately stop using these framing saws and take them to a DeWalt/Black & Decker service center for a free repair.

Injuries.Name: In all, six children have died in Playskool Travel-Lite portable cribs.

Distributors.Name: Kolcraft Enterprises Inc., of Chicago, Ill.

Hazards.Name: The cribs have rotating top rail hinges. These top rails can collapse, entrapping children and suffocating them.

Remedies.Name: Despite a nationwide effort over the past five years to alert the public about this recall, some of the 11,000 cribs originally sold could still be in use. To get these products back, Kolcraft and Playskool are doubling the reward for each returned crib from $60 to $120. In addition to the $120 reward, Kolcraft and Playskool, a subsidiary of Hasbro, are taking further steps to get the word out, including mailings to daycare centers, notices in new products and posting of details regarding the reward on Hasbro's web site at www.hasbro.com under Consumer Affairs Safety Message. Consumers who own these cribs should stop using them immediately. Anyone who sees one in a day care center, at a baby-sitters, in the home of a friend or relative, or at a garage sale or secondhand store, should inform the caregiver or seller about the recall and reward.

Description: The units have either black or white finishes, and glass-front doors. They were sold as three-piece sets, with two side piers and one connecting bridge, or as individual pieces. The side piers are 79 inches high and 24 inches wide, and the bridge is 38 inches wide.
Title: Entertainment Units Recalled by AIG Designs Holding
ConsumerContact: To schedule a service visit or for more information, call Sears at (800) 215-9167 anytime.

Injuries.Name: CPSC and AIG are not aware of any injuries or incidents caused by these units.

Manufacturers.Name: AIG Designs Holding Inc., of Alpharetta, Ga.

Retailers.Name: Sears stores nationwide sold the entertainment units, from October 1997 to March 1998. The three-piece set cost about $999. Each side pier cost about $450 individually and the bridge piece cost about $200.

Hazards.Name: The light fixture in these units can have exposed wiring, which could cause a fire or cause serious shock or electrocution.

Remedies.Name: Consumers should unplug the light fixtures immediately and call Sears to schedule a free, in-home service visit to replace the fixtures.

Description: These soldering irons were sold under the Electro-Tek brand name, and have part number 10764W. Both the brand name and part number are written only on the packaging. The soldering iron has a black plastic handle and is packaged on a white card with black, yellow and red accents. There is a silver label on the soldering irons with "UL" written in red. Electro-Tek soldering irons with different part numbers are not affected by this recall.
Title: Soldering Irons Recalled by Custom Accessories
ConsumerContact: For more information, consumers should call Custom Accessories Inc. toll free at (800) 962-6676 between 8:30 a.m. and 5:00 p.m. CST Monday through Friday.

Images.Caption: Recalled Electro-Tek Soldering Iron in package

Injuries.Name: None reported.

Retailers.Name: They were sold exclusively in Walmart stores nationwide, between October 1998 and November 1998, for about $5.

Importers.Name: Custom Accessories Inc., of Niles, Ill.

Hazards.Name: The internal connections in the soldering iron are not insulated, presenting a shock and electrocution hazard.

Remedies.Name: Consumers should stop using the soldering iron immediately and return it to Walmart for a refund or a replacement soldering iron.

Description: The "Henry" Gym Sets, model #68 includes two swings and a glider. The gym set is chrome colored with a blue top horizontal bar.
Title: "Henry" Gym Sets Recalled by Menard
ConsumerContact: Consumers may call Menard Inc. toll-free at (888) 215-3349 anytime.

Injuries.Name: A three-year-old boy was thrown to the ground when the support tube on the gym set broke. He did not suffer any injuries.

Manufacturers.Name: Menard Inc., of Eau Claire, Wis.

Retailers.Name: The 18 Menard retail stores in the North Central region of the U.S. sold these gym sets, from July 1991 through August 1998, for about $50.

Hazards.Name: If assembled incorrectly, the glider support tube on these gym sets could bend or break, causing the riders to fall or be thrown from the glider.

Remedies.Name: Consumers should not allow children to ride on the gym set glider until they check if their gym set is assembled correctly. To determine this and to receive revised assembly instructions, consumers should call Menard Inc.

Description: The wooden cradle is for infants from birth to 3 months of age and attaches to an adult bed to keep the baby within arm's reach. It is painted white and comes with four wooden legs. Each leg has three segments to adjust the height of the cradle.
Title: Bedside Cradles Recalled by W.C. Redmon
ConsumerContact: Consumers may call Redmon collect at (765) 473-6683 Monday through Friday between 9 a.m. and 6 p.m. EST. Consumers can also write to W.C. Redmon Co., P.O. Box 7, Peru, Ind. 46970.

Injuries.Name: Redmon has received about 50 reports of the cradles' legs becoming loose or separating, including two reports of cradles tipping. No injuries have been reported.

Manufacturers.Name: W.C. Redmon Co., of Peru, Ind.

Retailers.Name: Infant product catalogs, including One Step Ahead and Popular Club, and juvenile product stores, including Babies R Us and several small independent stores, sold the cradles nationwide, for about $149, beginning in February 1998.

Hazards.Name: The legs on the cradles can become loose and can separate, causing the cradle to tip.

Remedies.Name: Consumers should stop using the Cuddle Me Close cradle immediately and call Redmon for free replacement legs.
